title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The last two caches get a ceiling
summary: Semantic tokens kept the colouring of every file visited, 892 635 words of it on a real project. All three per file caches now drop the oldest file instead of emptying themselves.

highlights.title: Semantic tokens stop hoarding
highlights.description: Measured over a real Android project of 5088 files: 5088 entries holding 892 635 words of token data, for files that had long since left the screen. It now keeps 64.

highlights.title: Oldest file out, not the whole map
highlights.description: Emptying the map would have made every open editor recompute at once, which for semantic tokens means a visible repaint. The oldest entry goes instead, so what you are looking at keeps its answer.

highlights.title: One rule for the three caches
highlights.description: A single shared helper caps all of them, so they cannot drift apart again. That drift is exactly how the folding cache had been missed while its sibling was capped.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The sealed when coverage lens held 3187 entries to show 207 lenses; it gets the same ceiling.
Checked on the repository benchmark: no measurable change to folding or semantic token timing.
